### meter_ext_fast_meter_refund (hub doc_meter_fast_meter_refund_desk_guide; baseline doc_meter_fast_meter_refund_computation)
- **Rule head.** Carried verbatim: company test by type method classifies fast; recorded on the adjustment record as a refund on the calculation date.

The same-form restatement "so long as a repeat test fee owed … is not standing on the meter's metering charges, the refund amount is not yet fixed" is in the same document.   The strength matches.
- **Baseline.** Carried in full: counted-back bills, half reach-back, type refund limit, E + PSCR, factor, LPC and interest each 0.00, + standing repeat fees, threshold. Worked example recomputed (61.17; 106.17).

  - fast_refund_demand_basis: three tiers. Complete.
  - fast_refund_late_charges: GS/GST/GD/LP × factor rounded, RS/RT/REV in full, none. The span sentence is carried as the source states it. Complete.

- **Tool contract.** post_fast_meter_refund_06e0a347 matches.

## kb_to_source

Every normative sentence of the 33 documents of these four policies and of the base documents above traces to a source atom or to an entailed restatement. Worked examples were recomputed: 61.17 / 106.17; the interest table 1.28 / 0.32 / 0.16 / 0.58; 0.63 and 0.45 LPC; 73.17 / 38.17 / 1.53 / 0.25; 735.00; 225.00 / 300.00; 500.00 / 190.00; 19 months; the count examples. **No addition, rewrite or omission was found that the source does not carry.**

Prerequisite-side specific checks:
- (i) No cross-problem operational guidance. Each tool name appears only in its own hub.
- (ii) No opening world state written as policy fact.

Policy-side notes (reported, not counted against the documents):
- **N1.** Orphaned adjustment-basis variant parameters rendered as live "bases" in doc_meter_billing_adjustment_limits_by_meter_type, as in task 0/N1. Here this also includes the row "Usage basis for a meter found not registering … priced at the rates of the affected bills", which reads against the in-force NR baseline ("prior-year bills, as billed"). A reader resolves it through retired clause (d). The root cause is on the policy side.
- **N2 (stale parameter semantics in an illustration).** The parameter_schema description of repeat_test_fee_usd ("Fee for a customer-requested test beyond the free allowance when the meter is found accurate") was not updated when meter_ext_repeat_test_fee overwrote the flat-fee clause. doc_meter_accuracy_test_terms_schedule follows that description in its "Hypothetical illustration": "A customer-requested test of an AMI Interval Demand Meter … where it is chargeable as a repeat test, carries the 150.00 repeat test fee of that type." Read as the amount charged, this restates the retired flat fee. Under the in-force factors, an IDM (always secondary-voltage Schedule GD) repeat test fee is never a flat 150.00: the base already carries the 40.00 demand-register check, and witnessing adds 60.00 in the field. The source itself still defines the parameter this way, so per audit discipline the documents are not re-judged on this basis. It is reported here with its location so the coordinator can decide. It does not affect task 1 (PMI) numbers.
- **N3.** Cross-product figure visibility (LP minimum billing demand 500 kW, demand charge 16.27 USD/kW) as in task 0/N3.
- **N4 (span wording).** The LPC factors' "counted from the handling date as the covered bills are" is the source's own phrase. Source compute selects both bills and LPCs in whole months reckoned from NOW. The KB carries it faithfully. The blind audit flagged it as the one place a reader must pick between 3- and 4-month spans. The doc's second sentence ("the same months, reckoned back from the handling date, as the bills the refund covers") settles it on 4, matching GT.

## bijection_verdict

**PASS.** All four extended policies (rules, baselines, 21 factor ladders with every tier and figure, params, three prerequisite edges, four tool contracts), the in-scope base policies and the retired surface correspond at the level of entailment. N1–N4 are policy-side or coverage notes. N2 is the most material of them and is flagged for the coordinator. First revision.

## dependency_form

- Prerequisite sentences are verbatim on the blocked side only:
  - fast -> repeat fee: doc_meter_fast_meter_refund_desk_guide
  - referee refund -> fast refund and -> NR backbill: doc_meter_referee_refund_settlement_acceptance
  Their same-form restatements and record-table rows ("The repeat test fees standing on the meter"; "The fast-meter refund, once recorded …") are state descriptions in the same documents. No action, performer, tool or route is named beside them.
- The depended-on documents never mention who waits on them. The repeat-fee docs do not mention refunds or settlements. The fast-refund docs do not mention the referee settlement. The NR docs do not mention any refund. Two terms appear in another policy's baseline formula: "repeat test fee standing on the meter's metering charges" in the fast and referee-refund computations, and "refund already standing" in the referee-refund computation. These are the source's own formula terms, not a second statement of an edge.
- No aggregated chain, checklist or ordered step list across problems, and no cross-problem FAQ or named-mistake contrast. Pattern and meaning scan as for task 0.
- Titles are general ("Customer Care Note on Metering Service Referee Refund Settlements", "Metering Service Reporting Share for Customer-Reported Stopped Meters", …). None mirrors Riverbend's plant and warehouse situation.
- Computation documents carry no modifier hint. Factor documents state ladders as rules. Observation, not a finding: the two interest documents add "a bill whose billing period ended after the company test date is not [counted]". That faithfully renders "bills counted back from the company test date" and names no document or factor, so it is not counted as a pointer.
- Findability: the warehouse hop is reachable from the customer-wide find_meter_tests return (`non_registering`) through the words "not registering" and "non-registering backbill". The repeat-fee hop is reachable from "repeat test fee" and "metering charges", plus chargeability.
- Blind hop marks: all three are state-derived.

**PASS** (no KB-EXPLICIT finding).
